calls.why: I argued this one yesterday on a fatigue case built on 'fifth session in six days' and I withdraw it: he did not train on 2026-09-18, so tonight is the fifth session in seven days and the premise no longer holds. No new lifting has been logged since 2026-09-17, so I have no new reason to move the number. Two facts I am handing over rather than acting on: his only exposure to this movement since the gym change is 2026-09-08, where he logged three sets and not four, and the slot is still named smith-incline-press while he wrote 'Barbell' on it — the new gym has no smith machine. Neither is a recovery objection to the load.

The 157.5 asked for tonight sits under what he handled three days before the last log — 165x10 twice on 2026-09-14 — so the ask is not above his demonstrated capacity on this machine. The 11 and 10 he got at 157.5 on 2026-09-08 were his first session on it after the gym change. No recovery objection.

This is my one departure, and it is here because my own call yesterday rested on a statement that is false. I wrote that 2026-08-14 and 2026-09-08 showed 'no rep decay inside either session' and held on that basis. Both sessions decayed: 2026-08-14 was 14, 13, 12 and 2026-09-08 was 14, 13, 13. He has never completed three flat sets of 15 at this gym; the single flat 15/15/15 in the log is 2026-08-17, before the move. Asking for 15, 15, 15 is asking him to break a decay pattern on all three sets at once on the strength of a premise nobody checked. I am not asking for less than he did — 15/14/13 is plus one on set one, plus one on set two, and level with his best set three. Weight is unchanged.

45 lb moved from 8 reps for three sets on 2026-08-27 to 9 reps for three sets on 2026-09-08, flat across every set both times. Reps rising at a fixed load is the opposite of an under-recovery signal. Nothing new since the last review.

I checked whether three sets at 100 was a jump from the two sets he logged on 2026-09-08, and it is not: on 2026-09-14 he completed three flat sets of 12 at 99.2 lb with no decay. The three-set shape at this load is already proven and the packet is only asking one more rep. No objection.

55 lb produced 11, 10, 9 on 2026-09-08 and 12, 10, 9 on 2026-09-14. That is a normal within-session drop at a fixed load, repeated consistently, not accumulating fatigue. Load is unchanged tonight and no new session has been logged, so I have nothing to add.

I was wrong here yesterday: I asked for 45x12 twice when he had already completed 45x13 and 45x12 on 2026-09-08, which would have walked a stalled lift backwards. I am not re-arguing it and I am not proposing a number. One fact stays on the table without a change attached: set two on this lift has fallen below set one every time it has been logged, including 52.5/47.5/47.5 on 2026-08-17, so a flat 14 and 14 is a shape he has not yet produced. That belongs to whoever owns the ramp, not to me.
